skills.name: apply_bezout_theorem_to_intersections
skills.description: Use Bézout's theorem to compute the number of intersection points of two projective varieties when they intersect transversely, by multiplying their degrees.
skills.preconditions: Two projective subvarieties V,W ⊂ ℙⁿ defined by homogeneous equations, with no common component and intersecting properly (i.e., dimensions add to ≤ n).
skills.postconditions: The total number of intersection points counted with multiplicity equals deg(V)·deg(W).
skills.example: In ℙ², a line (degree 1) and a smooth cubic curve (degree 3) intersect in exactly 3 points (counted with multiplicity) by Bézout.

skills.name: compute_tangent_condition_via_dual_curve
skills.description: Translate the condition that a curve C is tangent to a fixed curve D into the condition that the point representing C lies on the dual variety D^∨ in the dual projective space.
skills.preconditions: A smooth projective plane curve D ⊂ ℙ² and a family of curves parametrized by a projective space (e.g., conics by ℙ⁵). The dual curve D^∨ ⊂ (ℙ²)^∨ is defined as the closure of the set of tangent lines to D.
skills.postconditions: A curve C from the family is tangent to D if and only if the corresponding point in the parameter space maps to a line lying in D^∨, i.e., satisfies the defining equations of D^∨.
skills.example: For a smooth cubic D ⊂ ℙ², the dual curve D^∨ is a degree 6 curve in the dual plane; a line ℓ is tangent to D exactly when the point representing ℓ in (ℙ²)^∨ lies on D^∨.

skills.name: determine_degree_of_finite_map_via_generic_fiber
skills.description: Compute the degree of a finite morphism by counting the number of points in a geometric generic fiber.
skills.preconditions: A morphism f : X → Y between irreducible varieties that is finite (hence proper with finite fibers) and dominant.
skills.postconditions: deg(f) = # (X_η) where X_η is the fiber over the generic point η of Y (geometric generic fiber).
skills.example: The map ℙ¹ → ℙ¹ given by t ↦ t² is finite of degree 2 because over the generic point the fiber consists of two distinct points.

skills.name: use_lang_weil_estimate_for_point_counts
skills.description: Apply the Lang–Weil estimate to relate the number of ℱ_q‑rational points on a geometrically irreducible variety to its dimension and degree, up to an error of O(q^{dim‑1/2}).
skills.preconditions: A geometrically irreducible projective variety X of dimension d defined over a finite field ℱ_q.
skills.postconditions: An asymptotic formula #X(ℱ_q) = q^d + O(q^{d-1/2}) holds, where the implied constant depends only on deg(X) and d.
skills.example: For a smooth plane conic (dimension 1, degree 2) over ℱ_q, Lang–Weil gives #C(ℱ_q) = q + 1 + O(√q), which matches the exact count q+1 when q is odd.

skills.name: average_fiber_size_over_finite_fields_equals_degree
skills.description: Use the fact that for a finite étale cover f : X → Y defined over ℤ, the average size of the fiber f^{-1}(y) over y ∈ Y(ℱ_p) tends to deg(f) as p → ∞ (Chebotarev/Deligne equidistribution).
skills.preconditions: A finite étale morphism f : X → Y of schemes of finite type over ℤ, with Y nonempty and geometrically irreducible.
skills.example: For the map ℙ¹ → ℙ¹, t ↦ t³, which is finite étale away from t = 0, the average number of preimages of a random point in ℙ¹(ℱ_p) approaches 3 as p → ∞.

skills.name: verify_finite_etale_locus_via_jacobian_nonvanishing
skills.description: Determine the open subset where a morphism is finite étale by checking that the Jacobian determinant does not vanish there.
skills.preconditions: A morphism f : X → Y of smooth varieties over a field, given locally by polynomial equations, and a point y ∈ Y where the fiber is finite.
skills.postconditions: The subset V ⊂ Y where the Jacobian matrix of the defining equations has full rank is open, and over V the morphism is étale (unramified and flat).
skills.example: For the map ℂ → ℂ, z ↦ z², the derivative 2z is nonzero away from z = 0, so the morphism is étale on ℂ∖{0}.

skills.name: parametrize_conics_by_symmetric_matrices
skills.description: Represent plane conics as zero loci of symmetric 3×3 matrices, turning the space of conics into ℙ⁵ via the six independent entries.
skills.preconditions: Working in ℙ² with homogeneous coordinates (x:y:z); a conic is defined by a homogeneous quadratic form Q(x,y,z) = [x y z]·M·[x y z]^T where M is a symmetric 3×3 matrix up to scaling.
skills.postconditions: The set of all conics corresponds to the projective space ℙ⁵ of symmetric matrices modulo scalar multiplication.
skills.example: The conic x² + yz = 0 corresponds to the matrix M = [[1,0,0],[0,0,½],[0,½,0]] (up to scaling).

skills.name: compute_resultant_to_eliminate_variables
skills.description: Use the resultant of two homogeneous polynomials to eliminate a variable and obtain a condition on the remaining coefficients, often expressing tangency or common zeros.
skills.preconditions: Two homogeneous polynomials f, g in variables x₀,…,x_n, where elimination of a variable (say x_n) is desired, and the coefficients lie in a polynomial ring.
skills.postconditions: The resultant Res_{x_n}(f,g) is a polynomial in the remaining coefficients that vanishes exactly when f and g have a common root in ℙ¹ (or when the corresponding curves are tangent along a line).
skills.example: For two binary quadratics f = a₀x² + a₁xy + a₂y² and g = b₀x² + b₁xy + b₂y², the resultant in x yields a condition a₀b₂ - a₁b₁ + a₂b₀ = 0, which characterizes when the two quadratics share a root.

skills.name: use_generic_smoothness_to_establish_flatness
skills.description: Apply the generic smoothness theorem to deduce that a morphism is flat over a dense open subset of the base where the fibers are smooth.
skills.preconditions: A morphism f : X → Y of finite type between Noetherian schemes over a field of characteristic 0 (or sufficiently large), with X reduced.
skills.postconditions: There exists a dense open U ⊂ Y such that f|_{f^{-1}(U)} is smooth, and consequently flat, over U.
skills.example: For the family of plane curves defined by F_t(x,y,z)=x²+y² - t z² in ℙ²×ℙ¹, generic smoothness implies that over t ≠ 0 the fibers are smooth conics, giving a flat morphism over ℙ¹∖{0}.

skills.name: apply_monodromy_transitivity_to_constancy_of_fiber_cardinality
skills.description: Use the transitivity of the geometric monodromy group of a finite étale cover to conclude that all geometric fibers have the same cardinality.
skills.preconditions: A finite étale morphism f : X → Y with Y connected (geometrically) and the associated monodromy action of π₁^{ét}(Y) on the fiber over a geometric point is transitive.
skills.postconditions: All geometric fibers of f have the same number of points, equal to deg(f).
skills.example: The cover given by adjoining a primitive n‑th root of unity to ℙ¹∖{0,∞} has Galois group (ℤ/nℤ)^{×} acting transitively on the n points of the fiber, so each fiber consists of n points.
